sections: 2.1 Flower — A Fascinating Organ of Angiosperms
2.2 Pre-fertilisation: Structures and Events (Microsporogenesis, Megasporogenesis, Pollination)
2.4 Post-fertilisation: Structures and Events (Endosperm, Embryo, Seed, Fruit)

cuetRelevance.pyqFrequency: Appears in 100% of tested CUET shifts (5-7 questions per shift)

summary30Seconds: Angiosperm microsporogenesis produces 2- or 3-celled pollen grains; megasporogenesis yields a monosporic 7-celled, 8-nucleate Polygonum-type embryo sac.
Double fertilisation is unique to angiosperms: Syngamy ($1n + 1n \to 2n$ Zygote) + Triple Fusion ($1n + 2n \text{ polar nuclei} \to 3n$ PEN / Primary Endosperm Nucleus).
Endosperm development precedes embryo development to provide nutrition; seeds can be albuminous (castor, wheat, maize) or non-albuminous (pea, gram, bean).

coreConcepts.title: Microsporogenesis & Pollen Grain Structure
coreConcepts.content:
The anther is typically bilobed and dithecous with four microsporangia. The anther wall comprises four distinct layers:
1. **Epidermis**: Outermost protective single layer.
2. **Endothecium**: Layer with $\alpha$-cellulosic fibrous bands that aid in hygroscopic dehiscence.
3. **Middle Layers**: 1–3 transient ephemeral nutritive layers.
4. **Tapetum**: Innermost layer with dense cytoplasm and polyploid/multinucleate cells that synthesizes sporopollenin, callase, and Pollenkitt.

Microspore mother cells (MMCs) undergo meiosis to produce microspore tetrads. Pollen grains have a two-layered wall:
- **Exine**: Made of **Sporopollenin** (one of the most resistant organic materials known; withstands high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali; no known enzyme degrades it). Possesses germ pores where sporopollenin is absent.
- **Intine**: Thin, continuous inner layer made of cellulose and pectin.
Over 60% of angiosperms shed pollen at the 2-celled stage (vegetative cell + generative cell); in the remaining <40%, the generative cell divides mitotically to form two male gametes before shedding (3-celled stage).
ncertPointers: Tapetum nourishes developing pollen grains and secretes sporopollenin.
Vegetative cell is bigger with abundant food reserve and irregular nucleus; generative cell floats in vegetative cell's cytoplasm.
Parthenium (carrot grass) came as a contaminant with imported wheat and causes pollen allergy and asthma.

coreConcepts.title: Megasporogenesis & The 7-Celled, 8-Nucleate Embryo Sac
coreConcepts.content:
The ovule (integumented megasporangium) is attached to the placenta via the funicle. The junction where the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle is the **hilum**.

A single Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC) in the micropylar region of the nucellus undergoes meiosis to form four megaspores. In most angiosperms, three degenerate at the micropylar end and only one functional megaspore at the chalazal end develops into the embryo sac (**Monosporic development**).

The nucleus of the functional megaspore undergoes three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions:
- 2-nucleate $\to$ 4-nucleate $\to$ 8-nucleate stage.
- Cytokinesis follows, organizing the classic **Polygonum-type embryo sac**:
  - **Egg apparatus** (Micropylar end): 2 Synergids (with filiform apparatus that guides pollen tube entry) + 1 Egg cell ($n$).
  - **Central cell**: Largest cell containing 2 polar nuclei in a large central vacuole.
  - **Antipodal cells** (Chalazal end): 3 cells that degenerate before or after fertilisation.
Total: **7 cells and 8 nuclei**.
ncertPointers: Filiform apparatus is cellular thickenings of the synergid wall at the micropylar tip.
Monosporic development: only one of the four megaspores gives rise to the female gametophyte.
Chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule; micropyle is the small opening where integuments do not cover.

coreConcepts.title: Outbreeding Devices, Pollination & Double Fertilisation
coreConcepts.content:
To prevent inbreeding depression caused by continued self-pollination, angiosperms have evolved outbreeding devices:
1. **Dichogamy**: Pollen release and stigma receptivity are non-synchronised (Protandry or Protogyny).
2. **Heterostyly**: Anther and stigma placed at different positions.
3. **Self-incompatibility**: Genetic mechanism preventing self-pollen from fertilising ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.
4. **Dicliny (Production of unisexual flowers)**: Monoecious plants (castor, maize) prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy; Dioecious plants (papaya, date palm) prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy.

**Double Fertilisation**:
1. **Syngamy**: One male gamete ($n$) fuses with egg cell ($n$) $\to$ Zygote ($2n$).
2. **Triple Fusion**: Second male gamete ($n$) fuses with the two polar nuclei ($n + n = 2n$) $\to$ Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, $3n$).
ncertPointers: Autogamy: Transfer of pollen within the same flower (cleistogamous flowers like Viola, Oxalis, Commelina are invariant autogamous and do not require pollinators).
Geitonogamy: Functionally cross-pollination (requires pollinator) but genetically similar to autogamy since pollen comes from the same plant.
Xenogamy: Genetically and functionally true cross-pollination.

coreConcepts.title: Post-Fertilisation: Endosperm, Embryo, Seed & Apomixis
coreConcepts.content:
**Endosperm Types**:
- **Free-nuclear endosperm**: PEN undergoes repeated nuclear divisions without cell wall formation (e.g., coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made of thousands of nuclei; surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm).

**Embryo Development**:
- In dicots: Zygote $\to$ Proembryo $\to$ Globular $\to$ Heart-shaped $\to$ Mature embryo with 2 cotyledons, embryonal axis (epicotyl terminating at plumule; hypocotyl terminating at radicle covered by root cap).
- In monocots (grasses): Single shield-shaped cotyledon called **Scutellum**, epicotyl with coleoptile, and radicle with coleorhiza.

**Apomixis & Polyembryony**:
- **Apomixis**: A form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, producing seeds without fertilisation (e.g., Asteraceae and grasses).
- In Citrus and Mango, nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac, and develop into multiple embryos (**Polyembryony**).
ncertPointers: False fruits: Thalamus contributes to fruit formation (e.g., apple, strawberry, cashew).
Parthenocarpic fruits: Fruit develops without fertilisation (e.g., banana); seedless.
Perisperm: Persistent residual nucellus found in black pepper and beet.

workedExamples.question: In an angiosperm plant, if the leaf cell has 24 chromosomes, determine the chromosome number in: (i) Pollen grain vegetative cell, (ii) Endosperm cell, (iii) Nucellar cell, and (iv) Synergid.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Leaf is a somatic tissue, so $2n = 24$, giving haploid number $n = 12$.
Step 2: (i) Pollen vegetative cell is haploid ($n$) = 12.
Step 3: (ii) Endosperm cell is triploid ($3n$) formed by triple fusion = $3 \times 12 = 36$.
Step 4: (iii) Nucellus is maternal ovule somatic tissue ($2n$) = 24.
Step 5: (iv) Synergid is a cell of female gametophyte ($n$) = 12. Correct sequence: 12, 36, 24, 12.

workedExamples.question: How many meiotic divisions and mitotic divisions are required to produce 100 viable seeds in a typical angiosperm?
solutionSteps: Step 1: 1 seed requires 1 male gametophyte (from 1 pollen grain) and 1 female gametophyte (from 1 megaspore).
Step 2: 1 microspore mother cell yields 4 functional pollen grains $\to 100 / 4 = 25$ meiotic divisions for male gametophytes.
Step 3: 1 megaspore mother cell yields 4 megaspores, but 3 degenerate, leaving only 1 functional megaspore $\to 100$ meiotic divisions for female gametophytes.

Step 5: For each female gametophyte, 1 functional megaspore undergoes 3 mitotic divisions ($100 \times 3 = 300$). For each pollen grain, 1 mitosis forms 2-celled pollen, and 1 generative cell mitosis forms 2 male gametes ($100 \times 2 = 200$ to $400$ mitotic). Total mitotic = 700. Option A is exact.

commonTraps.misconception: Students consider Geitonogamy to be genetically cross-pollination because pollen moves from one flower to another.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Genetically, geitonogamy is identical to autogamy because all flowers on the same plant share identical genes. Functionally, it is cross-pollination because it requires a pollinating agent.

commonTraps.misconception: Cleistogamous flowers open only at night to attract moths.
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Cleistogamous flowers NEVER open at all. They undergo assured autogamy even in the complete absence of pollinators.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following layers of the microsporangial wall is multinucleated and performs the function of nourishing developing pollen grains?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Tapetum is the innermost microsporangial wall layer. Its cells have dense cytoplasm and are generally multinucleate, nourishing developing microspores.

practiceQuestions.question: In a fertilised embryo sac, the haploid, diploid, and triploid structures respectively are:

options.text: Synergid, Zygote, and Primary Endosperm Nucleus

practiceQuestions.explanation: Synergid is haploid ($n$), Zygote is diploid ($2n$, formed by syngamy), and Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) is triploid ($3n$, formed by triple fusion).

practiceQuestions.question: Which one of the following plants prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Papaya is dioecious (male and female flowers are on separate plants). Hence, it prevents both autogamy (self-pollination in same flower) and geitonogamy (pollination between different flowers of same plant). Castor and maize are monoecious.

practiceQuestions.question: Persistent nucellus in the mature seed is called perisperm. It is found in:
practiceQuestions.explanation: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are persistent. This residual, persistent nucellus is called perisperm.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Cleistogamous flowers produce an assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators.
Reason (R): Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all, and anthers dehisce in close contact with stigma inside the flower bud.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Because cleistogamous flowers never open, autogamy is invariant and guaranteed, giving an assured seed set without needing any insects or wind.

practiceQuestions.question: The filiform apparatus is a characteristic feature of:
practiceQuestions.explanation: The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which play an important role in guiding pollen tubes into the synergid.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match Column I with Column II:
(a) Scutellum - (i) Monosporic 7-celled structure
(b) Perisperm - (ii) Single shield-shaped cotyledon of grasses
(c) Embryo sac - (iii) Residual persistent nucellus
(d) Coleorhiza - (iv) Undifferentiated sheath covering radicle
practiceQuestions.explanation: Scutellum is the grass cotyledon (ii); Perisperm is persistent nucellus (iii); Embryo sac is 7-celled 8-nucleate (i); Coleorhiza protects root cap/radicle (iv).

practiceQuestions.question: What is the ploidy of cells of nucellus, MMC, functional megaspore, and female gametophyte respectively?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Nucellus is maternal ovule tissue ($2n$); Megaspore Mother Cell undergoes meiosis ($2n$); Functional megaspore is product of meiosis ($n$); Female gametophyte develops from megaspore by mitosis ($n$).

practiceQuestions.question: Parthenocarpic fruits are produced by:

options.text: Fertilisation of flower by foreign pollen

practiceQuestions.explanation: Fruits that develop without fertilisation are called parthenocarpic fruits (e.g. banana). They are seedless.

practiceQuestions.question: Sporopollenin, the exine material of pollen grains, is synthesized by:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Tapetum synthesizes and secretes Ubisch bodies containing sporopollenin, forming the robust patterned exine of pollen grains.
